gloss: to start sliding; to get off to a start

definitions.gloss: to start sliding; to begin to slip
definitions.explanation: To begin sliding or slipping on a surface. Used for physical sliding motion.

definitions.gloss: to get off to a start; to launch; to get underway
definitions.explanation: Figuratively, to begin a new venture, season, or period. Often used with adjectives like 好調 (strong) or 順調 (smooth) to describe how something has started.

examples.japanese: {車|くるま}が{坂道|さかみち}で{滑|すべ}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: The car started sliding on the slope.

examples.japanese: {氷|こおり}の{上|うえ}で{足|あし}が{滑|すべ}り{出|だ}して{転|ころ}んだ。
examples.english: My feet started sliding on the ice and I fell.

examples.japanese: {雪|ゆき}がゆっくりと{屋根|やね}から{滑|すべ}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: The snow slowly began to slide off the roof.

examples.japanese: {新|しん}シーズンは{好調|こうちょう}に{滑|すべ}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: The new season got off to a strong start.

examples.japanese: {新商品|しんしょうひん}の{売|う}り{上|あ}げが{順調|じゅんちょう}に{滑|すべ}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: Sales of the new product got off to a smooth start.

examples.japanese: {新生活|しんせいかつ}は{不安|ふあん}もあったが、{思|おも}ったより{順調|じゅんちょう}に{滑|すべ}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I had some anxiety about my new life, but it got underway more smoothly than I expected.

notes:
USAGE:
Sense 2 is especially common in sports and business contexts. The noun form {滑|すべ}り{出|だ}し means "the start" or "the beginning" and is frequently used: {滑|すべ}り{出|だ}しは{好調|こうちょう}だ (the start is going well).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {好調|こうちょう}な{滑|すべ}り{出|だ}し (a strong start)
- {順調|じゅんちょう}に{滑|すべ}り{出|だ}す (to get off to a smooth start)
- {滑|すべ}り{出|だ}しが{良|い}い (to have a good start)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- スタートを{切|き}る: to make a start — more general
- {走|はし}り{出|だ}す: to start running — physical movement only
- {出足|であし}が{良|い}い: to have a good start — often for sales or attendance
